title: Majestic Double Sacrifice
transcript: Rook to B3 check. An ingenious idea. Not resigning because white is the god of chess himself and it is going to take more than one black queen to stop him. Black plays king to D4 getting out of the check. Now the white knight is hanging and there are a whole bunch of checks that the black queen can deliver at the right time. So it might seem like black is in control in this position. But white continues with the very precise knight to E6 check forcing the black king to go to C4 because it's the only square available. And now it seems like there is just no continuation. These checks are futile. The black king is just going to run away and there's no checkmate. White has failed and black is simply out of the woods, right? >> [laughter and gasps] >> Not exactly. White has the incredible and beautiful bishop to D5 check. A seemingly ridiculous and ludicrous sacrifice that has to be accepted because the king has no other legal moves. But once the bishop is taken, now white is left with only two pieces against this incredibly strong queen. And yet the only winning move is to sacrifice another one of the two with the beautiful knight to F4 [clears throat] check attacking the king and the queen at the same time meaning that if you move the king [music] I'm going to take the queen. But of course the knight can be taken. But this has placed the king and the queen in the perfect position to deliver rook to B5 check with a skewer. White wins the queen and the game.
